response.answer:
Understood—we’ll keep **Accounting** as the subject.

## Bachelor of Accounting

- **Credential:** Bachelor’s degree  
- **School:** School of Business + Media  
- **Campus:** Burnaby Campus  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time day stream or part-time Flexible Learning  
- **Program status:** Active  

The program is designed to provide an academic credential leading toward the **CPA designation**. It may also support progression to a Master of Professional Accounting or MBA. CPA alignment is academic preparation only; completing the program does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

### Academic requirements

The stored program requirements include:

- **60.0 academic credits**
- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the Advanced Technical Specialty pool**
- **36.0 General Education credits**
  - **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing**
  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - Additional General Education credits under the published category requirements

The Advanced Technical Specialty pool includes:

- **ACCG 6310 — Auditing and Assurance**
- **FMGT 7121 — Advanced Accounting**
- **FMGT 7210 — Advanced Management Accounting**
- **FMGT 7310 — Advanced Auditing**
- **FMGT 7410 — Taxation of Close Corporations**
- **FMGT 7510 — Advanced Finance**
- **FMGT 7520 — Business Valuation**
- **FMGT 7910 — The Business Environment**
- **FMGT 8121 — Contemporary Issues in Accounting**
- **FMGT 8610 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 1**
- **FMGT 8620 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 2**
- **FMGT 8920 — Case Writing Fundamentals**

You choose **seven courses** from that approved pool; the courses are not all cumulative requirements.

Optional work terms, available to eligible full-time domestic students, are:

- **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
- **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**

These optional work terms do not form part of the 60-credit academic requirement. They are unavailable to international students.

### Admission information

The stored admission requirements include:

- A BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually
- Minimum diploma GPA of **70%**
- English Studies 12 at **67%**, or equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two in the 62%–65% range
- A signed departmental pre-entry assessment and any assigned bridging or upgrading

The subject-sequence and pre-entry assessment requirements require institutional confirmation.

The program page states that international applicants may apply, subject to study-permit and other institutional or immigration requirements. Final PGWP decisions are made by IRCC.

**Program details:** https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

Understood—we’ll keep **Accounting** as the subject.

## Bachelor of Accounting

- **Credential:** Bachelor’s degree  
- **School:** School of Business + Media  
- **Campus:** Burnaby Campus  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time day stream or part-time Flexible Learning  
- **Program status:** Active  

The program is designed to provide an academic credential leading toward the **CPA designation**. It may also support progression to a Master of Professional Accounting or MBA. CPA alignment is academic preparation only; completing the program does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

### Academic requirements

The stored program requirements include:

- **60.0 academic credits**
- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the Advanced Technical Specialty pool**
- **36.0 General Education credits**
  - **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing**
  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - Additional General Education credits under the published category requirements

The Advanced Technical Specialty pool includes:

- **ACCG 6310 — Auditing and Assurance**
- **FMGT 7121 — Advanced Accounting**
- **FMGT 7210 — Advanced Management Accounting**
- **FMGT 7310 — Advanced Auditing**
- **FMGT 7410 — Taxation of Close Corporations**
- **FMGT 7510 — Advanced Finance**
- **FMGT 7520 — Business Valuation**
- **FMGT 7910 — The Business Environment**
- **FMGT 8121 — Contemporary Issues in Accounting**
- **FMGT 8610 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 1**
- **FMGT 8620 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 2**
- **FMGT 8920 — Case Writing Fundamentals**

You choose **seven courses** from that approved pool; the courses are not all cumulative requirements.

Optional work terms, available to eligible full-time domestic students, are:

- **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
- **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**

These optional work terms do not form part of the 60-credit academic requirement. They are unavailable to international students.

### Admission information

The stored admission requirements include:

- A BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually
- Minimum diploma GPA of **70%**
- English Studies 12 at **67%**, or equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two in the 62%–65% range
- A signed departmental pre-entry assessment and any assigned bridging or upgrading

The subject-sequence and pre-entry assessment requirements require institutional confirmation.

The program page states that international applicants may apply, subject to study-permit and other institutional or immigration requirements. Final PGWP decisions are made by IRCC.

**Program details:** https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

## Bachelor of Accounting overview

The **Bachelor of Accounting** is an active, in-person program at the **Burnaby Campus**, offered through either full-time daytime study or part-time Flexible Learning.

Students complete **60 academic credits**, including:

- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool**
- **36 General Education credits**, including **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing** and **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**

Optional work terms include **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**; they are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit academic requirement.

The program provides academic preparation toward pathways such as the CPA designation, a Master of Professional Accounting, or an MBA; it does not itself award professional certification.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

## Bachelor of Accounting

- **Credential:** Bachelor’s degree  
- **School:** School of Business + Media  
- **Campus:** Burnaby Campus  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time day stream or part-time Flexible Learning  
- **Program status:** Active  

The program is designed to provide an academic credential leading toward the **CPA designation**. It may also support progression to a Master of Professional Accounting or MBA. CPA alignment is academic preparation only; completing the program does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

### Academic requirements

The stored program requirements include:

- **60.0 academic credits**
- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the Advanced Technical Specialty pool**
- **36.0 General Education credits**
  - **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing**
  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - Additional General Education credits under the published category requirements

The Advanced Technical Specialty pool includes:

- **ACCG 6310 — Auditing and Assurance**
- **FMGT 7121 — Advanced Accounting**
- **FMGT 7210 — Advanced Management Accounting**
- **FMGT 7310 — Advanced Auditing**
- **FMGT 7410 — Taxation of Close Corporations**
- **FMGT 7510 — Advanced Finance**
- **FMGT 7520 — Business Valuation**
- **FMGT 7910 — The Business Environment**
- **FMGT 8121 — Contemporary Issues in Accounting**
- **FMGT 8610 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 1**
- **FMGT 8620 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 2**
- **FMGT 8920 — Case Writing Fundamentals**

You choose **seven courses** from that approved pool; the courses are not all cumulative requirements.

Optional work terms, available to eligible full-time domestic students, are:

- **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
- **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**

These optional work terms do not form part of the 60-credit academic requirement. They are unavailable to international students.

### Admission information

The stored admission requirements include:

- A BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually
- Minimum diploma GPA of **70%**
- English Studies 12 at **67%**, or equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two in the 62%–65% range
- A signed departmental pre-entry assessment and any assigned bridging or upgrading

The subject-sequence and pre-entry assessment requirements require institutional confirmation.

The program page states that international applicants may apply, subject to study-permit and other institutional or immigration requirements. Final PGWP decisions are made by IRCC.

  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - Additional General Education credits under the published category requirements

- **FMGT 7910 — The Business Environment**

- **FMGT 8610 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 1**
- **FMGT 8620 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 2**

The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

conversation.content: I'm exploring Accounting bachelor's degree. Please keep that as our subject.

Understood—we’ll keep **Accounting** as the subject.

## Bachelor of Accounting

- **Credential:** Bachelor’s degree  
- **School:** School of Business + Media  
- **Campus:** Burnaby Campus  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time day stream or part-time Flexible Learning  
- **Program status:** Active  

The program is designed to provide an academic credential leading toward the **CPA designation**. It may also support progression to a Master of Professional Accounting or MBA. CPA alignment is academic preparation only; completing the program does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

### Academic requirements

The stored program requirements include:

- **60.0 academic credits**
- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the Advanced Technical Specialty pool**
- **36.0 General Education credits**
  - **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing**
  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - Additional General Education credits under the published category requirements

The Advanced Technical Specialty pool includes:

- **ACCG 6310 — Auditing and Assurance**
- **FMGT 7121 — Advanced Accounting**
- **FMGT 7210 — Advanced Management Accounting**
- **FMGT 7310 — Advanced Auditing**
- **FMGT 7410 — Taxation of Close Corporations**
- **FMGT 7510 — Advanced Finance**
- **FMGT 7520 — Business Valuation**
- **FMGT 7910 — The Business Environment**
- **FMGT 8121 — Contemporary Issues in Accounting**
- **FMGT 8610 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 1**
- **FMGT 8620 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 2**
- **FMGT 8920 — Case Writing Fundamentals**

You choose **seven courses** from that approved pool; the courses are not all cumulative requirements.

Optional work terms, available to eligible full-time domestic students, are:

- **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
- **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**

These optional work terms do not form part of the 60-credit academic requirement. They are unavailable to international students.

### Admission information

The stored admission requirements include:

- A BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually
- Minimum diploma GPA of **70%**
- English Studies 12 at **67%**, or equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two in the 62%–65% range
- A signed departmental pre-entry assessment and any assigned bridging or upgrading

The subject-sequence and pre-entry assessment requirements require institutional confirmation.

The program page states that international applicants may apply, subject to study-permit and other institutional or immigration requirements. Final PGWP decisions are made by IRCC.

The program provides academic preparation toward pathways such as the CPA designation, a Master of Professional Accounting, or an MBA; it does not itself award professional certification.

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

request.instructions: You are Asteris, an academic advisor for the institution. The question has been routed as PROGRAM_INFO. Use the provided tools for every factual claim about courses, prerequisites, eligibility, or program progress. Never guess policy. If no tool can verify a factual or policy claim, say that it cannot be verified from the available Asteris data. Internal IDs are implementation details: never ask a student for a program ID. Course codes are normal student-facing information: whenever a course is named or returned, show its display_course_code alongside its course_name. Canonical course_id values are internal lookup keys; never show them when a display_course_code is available. Program IDs may be omitted in normal prose, but when the current question explicitly requests program IDs or codes, return the real program_id. Resolve course and program names with the search tools. When eligibility or progress requires a program that has not been identified, ask naturally which program the student is taking. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Be concise and clear. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For graduation questions, call evaluate_program_curriculum when available and prefer it over individual course role labels. Department approval applies to CMGT 8800 and CMGT 8810, not CMGT 8700. CMGT 8700 itself requires the stored coursework-completion rule, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor. The standard Liberal Studies component totals 12 credits. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. A resolved active program is authoritative for every program-specific tool. Never substitute a different program because a search is empty or irrelevant. Never invent application, acceptance, reapplication, enrolment, or document timing. For a current student asking about another pathway, explain only stored pathway and curriculum facts; label unstored transition or reapplication rules unknown. Answer yes/no and discovery questions concisely unless the student asks to list, show, browse, compare, or explain. Clearly label any inference, or omit it. uses exactly the same tools and rules as English. Respond entirely in the language of the current student question: English. Conversation history may provide subject or entity context but must never determine or carry over the response language. Keep co-op work terms, practical-work hours, and academic level progression separate. A level explicitly named in the current question overrides unrelated levels in history; never offer progression to another level.

conversation.content: I'm exploring Accounting bachelor's degree. Please keep that as our subject.

Understood—we’ll keep **Accounting** as the subject.

## Bachelor of Accounting

- **Credential:** Bachelor’s degree  
- **School:** School of Business + Media  
- **Campus:** Burnaby Campus  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time day stream or part-time Flexible Learning  
- **Program status:** Active  

The program is designed to provide an academic credential leading toward the **CPA designation**. It may also support progression to a Master of Professional Accounting or MBA. CPA alignment is academic preparation only; completing the program does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

### Academic requirements

The stored program requirements include:

- **60.0 academic credits**
- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the Advanced Technical Specialty pool**
- **36.0 General Education credits**
  - **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing**
  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - Additional General Education credits under the published category requirements

The Advanced Technical Specialty pool includes:

- **ACCG 6310 — Auditing and Assurance**
- **FMGT 7121 — Advanced Accounting**
- **FMGT 7210 — Advanced Management Accounting**
- **FMGT 7310 — Advanced Auditing**
- **FMGT 7410 — Taxation of Close Corporations**
- **FMGT 7510 — Advanced Finance**
- **FMGT 7520 — Business Valuation**
- **FMGT 7910 — The Business Environment**
- **FMGT 8121 — Contemporary Issues in Accounting**
- **FMGT 8610 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 1**
- **FMGT 8620 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 2**
- **FMGT 8920 — Case Writing Fundamentals**

You choose **seven courses** from that approved pool; the courses are not all cumulative requirements.

Optional work terms, available to eligible full-time domestic students, are:

- **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
- **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**

These optional work terms do not form part of the 60-credit academic requirement. They are unavailable to international students.

### Admission information

The stored admission requirements include:

- A BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually
- Minimum diploma GPA of **70%**
- English Studies 12 at **67%**, or equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two in the 62%–65% range
- A signed departmental pre-entry assessment and any assigned bridging or upgrading

The subject-sequence and pre-entry assessment requirements require institutional confirmation.

The program page states that international applicants may apply, subject to study-permit and other institutional or immigration requirements. Final PGWP decisions are made by IRCC.

**Program details:** https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/
Give me a short overview.

## Bachelor of Accounting overview

The **Bachelor of Accounting** is an active, in-person program at the **Burnaby Campus**, offered through either full-time daytime study or part-time Flexible Learning.

Students complete **60 academic credits**, including:

- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool**
- **36 General Education credits**, including **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing** and **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**

Optional work terms include **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**; they are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit academic requirement.

The program provides academic preparation toward pathways such as the CPA designation, a Master of Professional Accounting, or an MBA; it does not itself award professional certification.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor’s Degree—the Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc)**. The program provides academic preparation toward the **CPA designation**, but does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Where would I study?

You would study at **BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**. The program is delivered **in person**, with either **full-time daytime study** or **part-time Flexible Learning**.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Be concise and clear. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. conversation.content: Give me a short overview.

## Bachelor of Accounting overview

The **Bachelor of Accounting** is an active, in-person program at the **Burnaby Campus**, offered through either full-time daytime study or part-time Flexible Learning.

Students complete **60 academic credits**, including:

- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool**
- **36 General Education credits**, including **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing** and **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**

Optional work terms include **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**; they are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit academic requirement.

The program provides academic preparation toward pathways such as the CPA designation, a Master of Professional Accounting, or an MBA; it does not itself award professional certification.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor’s Degree—the Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc)**. The program provides academic preparation toward the **CPA designation**, but does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Where would I study?

You would study at **BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**. The program is delivered **in person**, with either **full-time daytime study** or **part-time Flexible Learning**.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it online or in person?

It is **in person** at BCIT’s **Burnaby Campus**. You can study through either:

- **Full-time daytime study**
- **Part-time Flexible Learning**

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it full-time or part-time?

It offers **both options**:

- **Full-time:** Day stream  
- **Part-time:** Flexible Learning, allowing you to register course by course

The program is delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby Campus**. [Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

expectation.question: What should I know before applying?

response.answer:
Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements
You generally need:

- A **BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma**, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually.
- A minimum **70% diploma GPA**.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**; no more than two may be between **62% and 65%**.
- A signed departmental **pre-entry assessment**. BCIT may also assign bridging or upgrading.

The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require institutional or departmental confirmation, so verify them with BCIT before applying. The available program data does not specify application deadlines, required documents, or timing.

### Program format
- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**
- Maximum completion period: **seven years**

The academic requirement is **60 credits**, including **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**, seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool, and **36 General Education credits**. Optional work terms—**FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**—are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit requirement.

If you have an external diploma, equivalency is assessed individually and bridging may be required. If you are an international applicant, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting, and the optional work terms are unavailable.

[View the full program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements
You generally need:

- A **BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma**, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually.
- A minimum **70% diploma GPA**.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**; no more than two may be between **62% and 65%**.
- A signed departmental **pre-entry assessment**. BCIT may also assign bridging or upgrading.

The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require institutional or departmental confirmation, so verify them with BCIT before applying. The available program data does not specify application deadlines, required documents, or timing.

### Program format
- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**
- Maximum completion period: **seven years**

The academic requirement is **60 credits**, including **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**, seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool, and **36 General Education credits**. Optional work terms—**FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**—are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit requirement.

If you have an external diploma, equivalency is assessed individually and bridging may be required. If you are an international applicant, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting, and the optional work terms are unavailable.

[View the full program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

content.text:
Yes, international applicants can apply to the **Bachelor of Accounting**.

Key points:

- You must obtain a **valid BCIT study permit before starting the program**.
- The optional work-term courses are not available to international students:
  - **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
  - **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**
- The program page states that bachelor’s-degree graduates may be eligible to apply for a **Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**. However, you must meet all **IRCC** requirements, and final approval is at IRCC’s discretion.
- The available data does not provide additional international-specific application or document requirements. Please confirm those details with BCIT.

[View the full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

conversation.content: Where would I study?

You would study at **BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**. The program is delivered **in person**, with either **full-time daytime study** or **part-time Flexible Learning**.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it online or in person?

It is **in person** at BCIT’s **Burnaby Campus**. You can study through either:

- **Full-time daytime study**
- **Part-time Flexible Learning**

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it full-time or part-time?

It offers **both options**:

- **Full-time:** Day stream  
- **Part-time:** Flexible Learning, allowing you to register course by course

The program is delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby Campus**. [Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements
You generally need:

- A **BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma**, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually.
- A minimum **70% diploma GPA**.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**; no more than two may be between **62% and 65%**.
- A signed departmental **pre-entry assessment**. BCIT may also assign bridging or upgrading.

The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require institutional or departmental confirmation, so verify them with BCIT before applying. The available program data does not specify application deadlines, required documents, or timing.

### Program format
- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**
- Maximum completion period: **seven years**

The academic requirement is **60 credits**, including **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**, seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool, and **36 General Education credits**. Optional work terms—**FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**—are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit requirement.

If you have an external diploma, equivalency is assessed individually and bridging may be required. If you are an international applicant, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting, and the optional work terms are unavailable.

[View the full program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What about international applicants?

Yes, international applicants can apply to the **Bachelor of Accounting**.

Key points:

- You must obtain a **valid BCIT study permit before starting the program**.
- The optional work-term courses are not available to international students:
  - **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
  - **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**
- The program page states that bachelor’s-degree graduates may be eligible to apply for a **Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**. However, you must meet all **IRCC** requirements, and final approval is at IRCC’s discretion.
- The available data does not provide additional international-specific application or document requirements. Please confirm those details with BCIT.

[View the full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

response.answer:
No. Meeting the listed requirements does **not guarantee admission**. It means you may be eligible to apply to the Bachelor of Accounting, but BCIT must assess your application.

Requirements include the appropriate diploma or equivalent, a minimum **70% diploma GPA**, **English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent**, the subject-sequence averages, and a signed departmental pre-entry assessment. The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require confirmation by BCIT. The available program information does not state any admission guarantee or selection policy.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

Use the provided tools for every factual claim about courses, prerequisites, eligibility, or program progress. Never guess policy. If no tool can verify a factual or policy claim, say that it cannot be verified from the available Asteris data. Internal IDs are implementation details: never ask a student for a program ID. Course codes are normal student-facing information: whenever a course is named or returned, show its display_course_code alongside its course_name. Canonical course_id values are internal lookup keys; never show them when a display_course_code is available. Program IDs may be omitted in normal prose, but when the current question explicitly requests program IDs or codes, return the real program_id. Resolve course and program names with the search tools. When eligibility or progress requires a program that has not been identified, ask naturally which program the student is taking. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Be concise and clear. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For graduation questions, call evaluate_program_curriculum when available and prefer it over individual course role labels. Department approval applies to CMGT 8800 and CMGT 8810, not CMGT 8700. CMGT 8700 itself requires the stored coursework-completion rule, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor. The standard Liberal Studies component totals 12 credits. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. A resolved active program is authoritative for every program-specific tool. Never substitute a different program because a search is empty or irrelevant. conversation.content: Is it online or in person?

It is **in person** at BCIT’s **Burnaby Campus**. You can study through either:

- **Full-time daytime study**
- **Part-time Flexible Learning**

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it full-time or part-time?

It offers **both options**:

- **Full-time:** Day stream  
- **Part-time:** Flexible Learning, allowing you to register course by course

The program is delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby Campus**. [Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements
You generally need:

- A **BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma**, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually.
- A minimum **70% diploma GPA**.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**; no more than two may be between **62% and 65%**.
- A signed departmental **pre-entry assessment**. BCIT may also assign bridging or upgrading.

The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require institutional or departmental confirmation, so verify them with BCIT before applying. The available program data does not specify application deadlines, required documents, or timing.

### Program format
- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**
- Maximum completion period: **seven years**

The academic requirement is **60 credits**, including **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**, seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool, and **36 General Education credits**. Optional work terms—**FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**—are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit requirement.

If you have an external diploma, equivalency is assessed individually and bridging may be required. If you are an international applicant, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting, and the optional work terms are unavailable.

[View the full program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What about international applicants?

Yes, international applicants can apply to the **Bachelor of Accounting**.

Key points:

- You must obtain a **valid BCIT study permit before starting the program**.
- The optional work-term courses are not available to international students:
  - **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
  - **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**
- The program page states that bachelor’s-degree graduates may be eligible to apply for a **Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**. However, you must meet all **IRCC** requirements, and final approval is at IRCC’s discretion.
- The available data does not provide additional international-specific application or document requirements. Please confirm those details with BCIT.

[View the full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the listed requirements does **not guarantee admission**. It means you may be eligible to apply to the Bachelor of Accounting, but BCIT must assess your application.

Requirements include the appropriate diploma or equivalent, a minimum **70% diploma GPA**, **English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent**, the subject-sequence averages, and a signed departmental pre-entry assessment. The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require confirmation by BCIT. The available program information does not state any admission guarantee or selection policy.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

response.answer:
For the **Bachelor of Accounting**, these details require confirmation with BCIT or the relevant authority:

- **Subject-sequence averages:** Whether your five second-year averages meet the stated standard—normally **65%**, with no more than two between **62% and 65%**.
- **Pre-entry assessment:** Whether the signed departmental assessment is required in your case and whether BCIT will assign bridging or upgrading.
- **External diploma equivalency:** Whether a diploma from another institution is considered equivalent and whether bridging is required.
- **General Education requirements:** Whether your planned courses satisfy the required **36 General Education credits** and the published category distribution.
- **International-student rules:** Confirmation of study-permit requirements and the restriction preventing international students from taking **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**.
- **PGWP eligibility:** The program data says graduates may apply, but final eligibility and approval must be confirmed through **IRCC**.
- **CPA outcome:** The degree provides academic preparation or alignment toward CPA studies; it does **not** itself award CPA designation or licensure. Confirm current CPA requirements with CPA British Columbia.
- **Course sequencing:** Confirm the current Fall/Winter sequencing for full-time specialty courses.

The available data does not specify **application deadlines, required documents, processing timelines, selection procedures, or an admission guarantee**. These should also be confirmed directly with BCIT.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

User: Is it full-time or part-time?
Assistant: It offers **both options**:

- **Full-time:** Day stream  
- **Part-time:** Flexible Learning, allowing you to register course by course

The program is delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby Campus**. [Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
User: What should I know before applying?
Assistant: Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements
You generally need:

- A **BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma**, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually.
- A minimum **70% diploma GPA**.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**; no more than two may be between **62% and 65%**.
- A signed departmental **pre-entry assessment**. BCIT may also assign bridging or upgrading.

The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require institutional or departmental confirmation, so verify them with BCIT before applying. The available program data does not specify application deadlines, required documents, or timing.

### Program format
- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**
- Maximum completion period: **seven years**

The academic requirement is **60 credits**, including **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**, seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool, and **36 General Education credits**. Optional work terms—**FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**—are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit requirement.

If you have an external diploma, equivalency is assessed individually and bridging may be required. If you are an international applicant, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting, and the optional work terms are unavailable.

[View the full program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
User: What about international applicants?
Assistant: Yes, international applicants can apply to the **Bachelor of Accounting**.

Key points:

- You must obtain a **valid BCIT study permit before starting the program**.
- The optional work-term courses are not available to international students:
  - **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
  - **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**
- The program page states that bachelor’s-degree graduates may be eligible to apply for a **Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**. However, you must meet all **IRCC** requirements, and final approval is at IRCC’s discretion.
- The available data does not provide additional international-specific application or document requirements. Please confirm those details with BCIT.

[View the full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
User: Does that guarantee admission?
Assistant: No. Meeting the listed requirements does **not guarantee admission**. It means you may be eligible to apply to the Bachelor of Accounting, but BCIT must assess your application.

Requirements include the appropriate diploma or equivalent, a minimum **70% diploma GPA**, **English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent**, the subject-sequence averages, and a signed departmental pre-entry assessment. The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require confirmation by BCIT. The available program information does not state any admission guarantee or selection policy.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

The available data does not specify **application deadlines, required documents, processing timelines, selection procedures, or an admission guarantee**. These should also be confirmed directly with BCIT.

conversation.content: Is it full-time or part-time?

It offers **both options**:

- **Full-time:** Day stream  
- **Part-time:** Flexible Learning, allowing you to register course by course

The program is delivered **in person** at the **Burnaby Campus**. [Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements
You generally need:

- A **BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma**, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually.
- A minimum **70% diploma GPA**.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**; no more than two may be between **62% and 65%**.
- A signed departmental **pre-entry assessment**. BCIT may also assign bridging or upgrading.

The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require institutional or departmental confirmation, so verify them with BCIT before applying. The available program data does not specify application deadlines, required documents, or timing.

### Program format
- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**
- Maximum completion period: **seven years**

The academic requirement is **60 credits**, including **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**, seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool, and **36 General Education credits**. Optional work terms—**FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**—are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit requirement.

If you have an external diploma, equivalency is assessed individually and bridging may be required. If you are an international applicant, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting, and the optional work terms are unavailable.

[View the full program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What about international applicants?

Yes, international applicants can apply to the **Bachelor of Accounting**.

Key points:

- You must obtain a **valid BCIT study permit before starting the program**.
- The optional work-term courses are not available to international students:
  - **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
  - **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**
- The program page states that bachelor’s-degree graduates may be eligible to apply for a **Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**. However, you must meet all **IRCC** requirements, and final approval is at IRCC’s discretion.
- The available data does not provide additional international-specific application or document requirements. Please confirm those details with BCIT.

[View the full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the listed requirements does **not guarantee admission**. It means you may be eligible to apply to the Bachelor of Accounting, but BCIT must assess your application.

Requirements include the appropriate diploma or equivalent, a minimum **70% diploma GPA**, **English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent**, the subject-sequence averages, and a signed departmental pre-entry assessment. The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require confirmation by BCIT. The available program information does not state any admission guarantee or selection policy.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

In simple terms:

- You may be able to apply, but meeting the requirements does **not guarantee admission**.
- BCIT needs to confirm:
  - Whether your diploma is equivalent.
  - Whether your grades in the required subjects are high enough.
  - Whether you need bridging or upgrading.
  - Whether your courses meet the **36 General Education credits**.
  - The current course schedule and sequencing.
- If you are an international student, you need a valid BCIT study permit. You cannot take **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** or **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**.
- PGWP eligibility must be confirmed with **IRCC**.
- The program can prepare you for CPA studies, but it does not automatically grant a CPA designation.

BCIT has not provided verified details here about deadlines, required documents, processing times, selection procedures, or admission guarantees. Confirm those directly with BCIT:

[View the Bachelor of Accounting program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

conversation.content: What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, keep these points in mind:

### Admission requirements
You generally need:

- A **BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma**, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually.
- A minimum **70% diploma GPA**.
- **English Studies 12 with at least 67%**, or an equivalent qualification.
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**; no more than two may be between **62% and 65%**.
- A signed departmental **pre-entry assessment**. BCIT may also assign bridging or upgrading.

The subject-sequence averages and pre-entry assessment require institutional or departmental confirmation, so verify them with BCIT before applying. The available program data does not specify application deadlines, required documents, or timing.

### Program format
- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**
- Maximum completion period: **seven years**

The academic requirement is **60 credits**, including **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**, seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool, and **36 General Education credits**. Optional work terms—**FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**—are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit requirement.
